newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor hits new low on works, profit anxiety.
newsitem.headline: Iscor hits new low on works, profit anxiety.

text.p: Market anxiety over possible poor profits and operational glitches crushed Iscor shares to yet another year low on Thursday.
Analysts and dealers said gloom about the iron and steel producer's first quarter performance was weighing shares and had sent them down for the second consecutive day.
Iscor slumped to 292 cents from its previous 318 cents close, before recovering some losses and retracing to 300 cents.
Volumes were large with four million shares changing hands.

"The market is getting the impression that Iscor has had a poor first quarter and there has also been some talk of operational glitches at Vanderbijlpark," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
"They're implementing new equipment and machinery there and we're seeing the difficulty in that," he added, referring to Iscor's steel works at Vanderbijlpark.
Dealers said that a number of analysts had downscaled their year earnings forecasts.
"There's no smoke without a fire and something is obviously leaking out of the company that things are not going as well as could be hoped," another analyst told Reuters.

But market commentators said that the negative situation was likely to be short-term with new operations coming online soon and the commodity price cycle seen picking up in the next two to three years.
"The longer term picture for Iscor is quite good. There are new plants in the pipeline and this would combine with stronger commodity prices in two to three years time," an analyst said.
Iscor announced poor interim results in February, but said the second half of the year would be better. The company posted a half-year share of 6.5 cents from 17.6 cents previously.
